uncertainties.note: Speakers are untagged. Content points to Garrod (1285, 1294), Jamil (1286, 1288, 1290), the two freelance Vultures (1287, 1289, 1292, 1293) and a Londo Bell pilot reacting to the word Gundam (1295), but no identity was written into the English. 1285's 'too' reads the source as 'you as well are chasing Tiffa for her power'; the source has no explicit 'also', only the chasing-after nuance - a reviewer may prefer dropping 'too'.

'Our princess' is taken as Tiffa riding in the GX with its pilot, because 1294 answers with a refusal to hand Tiffa over. It could also be sarcasm aimed at the GX pilot. English keeps 'the one riding in the GX' without gender.
Source omits the subject ('seems [it] was not in time'); follows the Freeden-destroyed line 1300. 'We' supplied as minimal subject; an impersonal 'Too late, it seems...' is the alternative.

1303 'escort force silenced' does not say whose escorts. Slot order puts it directly after the Flail-struggling line (slot 87 -> 89), which suggests the allied Flail escort was wiped out (compare 00735/00736), but 1270 uses the same word for the ENEMY escorts around the field weapon, whose defeat would trigger 1271. Kept bare and neutral.
Whiny polite register and 'Captain' (kanchou, not the 'Captain' loanword used for Jamil) suggest the Nadesico B bridge (Hari to Ruri), likely a time-limit warning. Speaker not written in.
Object of 'protect' omitted in source; 'you' = Tiffa inferred from the 1313-1316 exchange.
Source is a bare 'complaints after surviving'; rendered as paired imperatives to avoid choosing we/you.
'Mobile suit modoki' (pseudo/imitation mobile suits) rendered 'mobile suit look-alikes'; refers to the New Federation mass-production machines from a Londo Bell viewpoint. No established term found.
Speaker uses 'boku-tachi'; could be a Freeden bridge crewman or Hari. Left untagged.
Both kanchou and the loanword kyaputen come out as 'Captain' in English; the source distinction (Ruri vs Jamil) is lost but context disambiguates.
